name: SN74LVC1T45DBVR
title: SN74LVC1T45: single-bit dual-supply bus transceiver, configurable voltage translation, 3-state outputs
summary: A one-bit, non-inverting level translator with a separate supply for each side, both 1.65 V to 5.5 V. Port A and the DIR pin follow VCCA, port B follows VCCB, and DIR sets which way data flows. If either supply is grounded both ports turn off, and Ioff keeps an unpowered part from passing current back. SN74LVC1T45DBVR is the SOT-23 (DBV) version on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: 420 Mbps (3.3 V to 5 V); 210 Mbps to 3.3 V; 140 Mbps to 2.5 V; 75 Mbps to 1.8 V
±24 mA at 3.3 V; ±32 mA at 4.5 V to 5.5 V
±2000 V HBM; ±1000 V CDM; ±200 V machine model

notes: All are SN74LVC1T45; the letters after it give the package (DBV SOT-23, DCK SC70, DPK USON, DRL SOT-5X3, YZP DSBGA) and the reel (R a large reel, T a small reel). E4, G4 and the .A or .B suffixes are further orderable codes of the same package and reel.

circuits.title: Unidirectional logic level shifting
circuits.description: A signal from a buffer in SYSTEM-2, powered from VCC2, crosses to a buffer in SYSTEM-1, powered from VCC1. VCCA is on VCC1 and VCCB on VCC2. DIR is grounded together with GND, which fixes the direction B to A: B is the input, with thresholds set by VCC2, and A drives the SYSTEM-1 buffer with VCC1 levels. VCC1 and VCC2 can each be anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V.

circuits.title: Bidirectional logic level shifting
circuits.description: One data line runs both ways between I/O-1 in SYSTEM-1 (on VCC1) and I/O-2 in SYSTEM-2 (on VCC2). VCCA is on VCC1 and VCCB on VCC2; A joins I/O-1 and B joins I/O-2. SYSTEM-1 drives DIR from its DIR CTRL output. Each side of the line has a pull-up, pull-down or bus hold, so the line sits at a known level while both ports are off during a change of direction; both sides use the same kind. The part has no output enable, so the two systems must not drive the line against each other when the direction turns round.

parts.value: I/O-1, SYSTEM-1 transceiver with DIR CTRL output

notes: R1 and R2 each meet the line at one point; where a pull-up or pull-down is used, its other end goes to that side's supply or to ground.

operation.text: One non-inverting buffer that can face either way between two ports, each with its own supply. Port A and the DIR pin run from VCCA; port B runs from VCCB. Both supplies may sit anywhere in 1.65 V to 5.5 V, so any pair of 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V logic can be joined. DIR high sends A to B; DIR low sends B to A. Data moves asynchronously, with no clock.
The input stages of both A and B are always on, whichever way DIR points. A data pin left without a high or low level draws extra ICC and ICCZ, so an unused input goes to its VCCI or to GND.
Highest data rates: 420 Mbps translating 3.3 V to 5 V, 210 Mbps translating to 3.3 V, 140 Mbps to 2.5 V and 75 Mbps to 1.8 V.
With the part unpowered its I/Os go high-impedance, so no damaging current flows back into it from a powered bus. The leakage that remains is the Ioff figure of the electrical characteristics.
If either supply is at ground while the other is still up, both ports go high-impedance; leakage at each pin is again bounded by Ioff.

The outputs are balanced CMOS push-pull stages that source and sink about equal currents: ±24 mA at 3.3 V. Their edges are fast into light loads, so line matching and the load need attention to stop ringing. An output can deliver more current than the part survives; two outputs may be joined for more drive, always inside the absolute maximum ratings.

Ground goes on first. After that the two supplies may come up or go down in any order and at any ramp rate without a glitch on the I/Os, so a downstream part does not see a false bit that could reset or misconfigure it.

There is no output-enable pin. To reverse a bidirectional line, both systems first stop driving it, DIR is changed, and only then does the new sender drive. While both ports are off the line is held by a pull-up, pull-down or bus hold, the same kind on both sides. The enable times in the switching tables give the wait from the DIR edge to a valid output.
The input range is set by the supply of whatever drives the part: a high must be above the input port's VIH and a low below its VIL. The output range is set by the supply of the side being driven.

Bypass both supplies with capacitors and keep signal traces short to limit loading. Pads on the signal lines for a load capacitor or pull-up resistor allow the rise and fall times to be tuned if the system calls for it. Example placement: a bypass capacitor at VCCA (pin 1) and at VCCB (pin 6), each between its supply via and a ground via; pin 2 grounded through a via to an inner ground plane; DIR (pin 5) tied to VCCA through a resistor; A (pin 3) from the controller and B (pin 4) to the system.
